title: Reading Comprehension
parentNote: This section tests reading and understanding. Read each passage TWICE with your child — once for the story, once for the details. Encourage them to find answers IN the passage, not from their imagination!
learnBullets: Answering questions based on **what you read**
learnItFirst:
**What is Reading Comprehension?**
It means reading a passage and understanding what it says. You will answer questions based on what is written.

**Tips for Reading Comprehension:**
1. **Read the passage carefully** — don't rush!
2. **Read the questions** — understand what is being asked
3. **Go back to the passage** — find the answer in the text
4. **Don't guess** — the answer is always in the passage!

**Types of Questions:**
- **Who** did something?
- **What** happened?
- **Where** did it happen?
- **When** did it happen?
- **Why** did it happen?

sections.name: Warm Up
sections.leadingContext:
**Read the passage and answer questions 1-5:**

> **The Lost Puppy**
> 
> One day, Riya found a small puppy near her house. The puppy was brown and had a red collar. It looked hungry and sad. Riya gave it some milk and bread. The puppy wagged its tail happily.
> 
> Riya's mother helped her put up posters in the neighborhood. Two days later, a little boy named Arjun came to their house. He was so happy to see his puppy! He thanked Riya and gave her a box of chocolates.

questions.content: What did Riya find near her house?
questions.why: "Riya found a small puppy near her house"

questions.content: What colour was the puppy?
What did Riya give the puppy?
questions.why: "Riya gave it some milk and bread"

questions.content: Who was the owner of the puppy?
questions.why: "a little boy named Arjun... his puppy"

questions.content: What did Arjun give Riya to thank her?

sections.name: Olympiad Practice
sections.leadingContext:
**Read the passage and answer questions 11-17:**

> **My Pet Parrot**
> 
> I have a pet parrot named Mitthu. He has beautiful green feathers and a red beak. Every morning, Mitthu wakes me up by saying "Good morning! Good morning!" He loves to eat sunflower seeds and apples.
> 
> Mitthu can say many words. He says "Hello" when visitors come and "Bye-bye" when they leave. Sometimes he copies the sound of our doorbell! My grandmother taught him to say "Ram-Ram" which makes everyone laugh.
> 
> I clean Mitthu's cage every Sunday. I give him fresh water daily. Mitthu is not just a pet — he is my best friend!

questions.content: What is the parrot's name?
What colour are Mitthu's feathers?
What does Mitthu say in the morning?
What does Mitthu like to eat?
questions.why: "loves to eat sunflower seeds and apples"

questions.content: Who taught Mitthu to say "Ram-Ram"?
When does the narrator clean Mitthu's cage?
What sound does Mitthu sometimes copy?
questions.trailingContext:
---

**Read the message and answer questions 18-21:**

> **Message on the refrigerator:**
> 
> Dear Rohan,
> 
> I have gone to the market. Your lunch is in the blue box inside the fridge. Heat it in the microwave for 2 minutes. Don't forget to drink your milk! I will be back by 5 o'clock.
> 
> Do your homework before watching TV.
> 
> Love,
> Mummy
> 
> P.S. – Your sister is at her friend's house.

questions.content: Where has Mummy gone?
Where is Rohan's lunch?

options.A: In the blue box in the fridge

questions.why: "in the blue box inside the fridge"

questions.content: What time will Mummy be back?
What should Rohan do before watching TV?
questions.trailingContext:
---

**Read the passage and answer questions 22-25:**

> **The Ant and the Dove**
> 
> One hot summer day, a tiny ant went to the river to drink water. Suddenly, a strong wind blew and the ant fell into the river. "Help! Help!" cried the ant.
> 
> A kind dove was sitting on a tree nearby. She saw the ant struggling in the water. Quickly, she dropped a leaf into the river. The ant climbed onto the leaf and floated safely to the shore.
> 
> A few days later, a hunter came to catch the dove. He pointed his net at the bird. The ant saw this and bit the hunter's foot hard! "Ouch!" shouted the hunter. The dove heard the noise and flew away to safety.
> 
> The ant and the dove became good friends. They learned that a friend in need is a friend indeed!

questions.content: Why did the ant go to the river?
questions.why: "went to the river to drink water"

questions.content: How did the dove save the ant?
questions.why: "she dropped a leaf into the river"

questions.content: How did the ant help the dove?
What is the lesson of this story?

options.A: A friend in need is a friend indeed
